new_statements.rule_in_words: Dagang Biao is described only as a 10-tone system (6 tones on smooth syllables: 54, 31, 35, 132, 34, 22; 4 on checked syllables: 55, 22, 34, 42) corresponding one-to-one with Shidong; no Dagang-specific statement about word stress exists in any opened source. The same Shidong-based grammar asserts for 'Biao' as a whole that there is no stress feature (p.50) and that prefixal 'affixable morphemes' (a55, to214, lak12) are unstressed with stress on the root, forming sesquisyllabic iambs (pp.76, 81, 83) -- i.e. tonal, no contrastive word stress, root/final-syllable prominence in prefix+root words -- but that rests on Shidong fieldwork, not Dagang.
new_statements.exceptions: None for Dagang. (Shidong: non-final syllables undergo tone sandhi, high tones -> 33, low tones -> 21, pp.56-57; prefixes unstressed.)
new_statements.domain_note: Dagang material in the opened sources is citation-form wordlist data (Hsiu 2013 first-hand; Liang 2024 sec. 2.9 second-hand from Liang & Zhang 2002). The 'no stress' sentence (p.50) sits in the monophthong section and most plausibly means no contrastive stress/tenseness/nasality on vowels; the affixation chapter describes word-internal prominence (unstressed prefix + stressed root).
new_statements.identity_note: daga1277 is Glottolog's split-off 'Dagang-Baoshan-Liangcun' (NOCODE_Dagang-Biao), created from Hsiu's 2013 report that Dagang 大岗 / Liangcun 梁村 (Huaiji) and Baoshan 保山村, Chang'an 长安镇 (Fengkai) Biao are mutually intelligible with each other but not with Shidong [biao1253] or Yonggu [yong1283] Biao; Hsiu 2014 calls it 'Northwestern Biao' (also Qiaotou), Yang 2023 the 'northern dialect' (Daliang + Chang'an). The only stress-related sentences found ('no.. stress in Biao', unstressed prefixes / stressed roots) come from Liang Jingui 2024, whose fieldwork variety is Shidong (Shuanglong village) = biao1253 and who treats Dagang as a mere 'vernacular' of one Biao language; her Dagang data are second-hand from Liang & Zhang 2002. No first-hand Dagang/Liangcun/Baoshan source that was opened says anything about stress.

sources.note: For Dagang: only tones (6 smooth + 4 checked: 54, 31, 35, 132, 34, 22; 55, 22, 34, 42), initial and final correspondences; nothing on stress. For 'Biao' generally (Shidong data): p.50 'There is no feature such as tenseness, nasal or stress in Biao'; p.76 affixable morphemes are 'slight sounds, with the stress on the root morphemes'; pp.81, 83 prefixes a55, to214, lak12 unstressed, 'half of the metrical foot' (sesquisyllable); pp.56-57 tone sandhi on non-final syllables.
